clue.text: Control unit is protected by fuse

indicators.note: something protected by another thing is enclosed within it, so the unit goes inside the fuse

parts.note: to fuse metals is to weld them
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: An electrician describes a control unit kept safe by a fuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield power or a tool is to handle it and have command over it.

clue.text: Sectarians establishing hideouts in the principality

indicators.note: the hideouts are placed in the principality, inside its letters

parts.note: Wales is traditionally called the Principality
dens are hideouts or lairs

explanation.surface: A religious sect sets up secret refuges inside a small country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Principality is a traditional name for Wales, the country of the UK whose heir to the throne is the Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Waldenses were a medieval Christian sect, followers of Peter Waldo, regarded as heretics.

clue.text: Improve morality of journalist if ending in debauchery

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist
taken as written

indicators.note: the ending of the word debauchery is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone wants to reform a reporter who might end up in dissolute living.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct or uplift someone morally and intellectually.

clue.text: An unusual little medicine has turned up — it's sweet and exotic

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole run of letters is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
rare means unusual
MED is a short form of medicine

explanation.surface: A rare dose of medicine comes back up, and it tastes sweet and foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'has turned up', turns the whole run A + RARE + MED, giving the answer read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a brown cane sugar named after a region of Guyana, so a sweetener from overseas.

clue.text: Bomb taken from ole bod dug out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb is unearthed by an old fellow digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ole bod' is a jokey spelling of 'old body', i.e. an old chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the wartime nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb.

clue.text: Man needs this girlfriend maybe for support

indicators.note: the clue says the word Man needs this answer to make a word for support, so what remains after removing it is wanted

parts.note: a mandate is an authority or backing given, as by voters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man wants a girlfriend to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Man needs this ... for support' as MAN + ? = MANDATE (backing, authority); the missing piece is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a person one is going out with, such as a girlfriend; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Drink shop's breach of the law — harbouring endless insects

indicators.note: the breach of the law harbours, or shelters, the insects inside it

parts.note: an offence is a breach of the law

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the insects word is dropped

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A liquor store breaks the law by being infested with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims LICE to LIC, which goes inside OFFENCE. The ''s' of 'shop's' stands for 'is'. An OFF-LICENCE is the British term for a shop licensed to sell alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is a British liquor store, licensed to sell alcohol for drinking off the premises.

clue.text: Area offering beer — look around first

indicators.note: first places the look-and-around pieces ahead of the beer

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
C is short for circa, Latin for around
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood serves beer, so take a look around it before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a place or setting where something happens.

clue.text: Dance leader, a star bursting on the scene

parts.note: a boss is a leader at work
a nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness

explanation.surface: A dancer who leads becomes an overnight star.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to samba.

clue.text: Aquatic bird showing up among icebergs

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing up means the letters read upwards
among signals that the bird is found inside the word icebergs

explanation.surface: A waterbird appears among floating ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'icebergs' run EBERG; read upwards it gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebes are diving water birds with lobed toes, found on lakes and ponds.

clue.text: Artistic theme frivolous, we hear — witty saying introducing poem

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is given by its sound

parts.note: light can mean frivolous, not serious
a mot is a witty remark, from bon mot, and it comes just before the poem
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A critic calls an artistic motif lightweight, then quotes a quip before a verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring theme in music or literature associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: Social class left out of stronghold

indicators.note: out of means the left letter is taken out of the stronghold

parts.note: a castle is a stronghold

explanation.surface: Someone of a certain rank is shut out of the fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the traditional Hindu system.

clue.text: Parts of insects, see, needing skill for retraction

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with one

indicators.note: retraction means drawing back, so the skill word is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An entomologist looks at insect parts and needs skill to pull them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Elytra are the hardened forewings of beetles, covering the delicate flight wings.

clue.text: Flower having a connection with flour?

definitions.text: Flower having a connection with flour?

parts.words: Flower having a connection with flour?
parts.note: a flower is read as a thing that flows, a stream of water, and the flour link points to the grinding works it drives

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders which blossom is related to baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a blossom; it is something that flows. A MILL-RACE is the channel of water that turns a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill-race is the current of water channelled to drive a mill wheel that grinds grain.

clue.text: A not-far-from-grand piece of furniture

parts.note: grand suggests a stately item, but it is a grand piano, and this seat sits close beside one

explanation.surface: An item of furniture that is nearly but not quite grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' wants to mean impressive; it is the grand piano, and the seat stands just next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano stool is the seat a pianist uses, placed right in front of the keyboard.

clue.text: Solemn person cries without hesitation the day of emperor's death

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cries surround the other pieces

parts.note: sobs are cries of distress
er is the sound of hesitation in speech
Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A serious person weeps without pausing on the anniversary of Caesar's murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it is the old sense 'outside'. The Ides (15 March) is the day Julius Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a humourless, serious-minded individual.

clue.text: Stopped suddenly and reared

definitions.meaning: to be pulled up short is to halt abruptly
raised as a child, as in well raised

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both halted abruptly and raised from childhood, two idiomatic senses.

clue.text: Animal has a run in retreat

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to flow is to run, as liquid does

explanation.surface: A beast scampers off in retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild carnivorous mammal of the dog family.

clue.text: Fish in the country without an employer to worry about?

definitions.text: without an employer to worry about?

indicators.note: the fish is placed in the country, inside its letters

parts.note: France is the country
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A fish living in the countryside has no boss to fret over.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works independently for several clients rather than for a single boss.

clue.text: Report of boy getting underweight — this is essential for growth

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are given by how they sound

parts.note: a boy is a son, and underweight is light

explanation.surface: News that a lad is losing weight, with a remark about what helps things grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants need sunshine for photosynthesis, so it drives their growth.

clue.text: Pollutant gets oxygen repeatedly restricted in street

indicators.note: the oxygen is confined within the street abbreviation
repeatedly means the oxygen symbol is used twice

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Smog-forming particles are trapped in a city road where the air keeps being shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Soot is black carbon dust from burning, a common air contaminant.

clue.text: Unsound chapter in a cleric's compilation

indicators.note: compilation signals the pieces are compiled into one, with the chapter set among the others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a curate is a junior cleric in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chapter in a churchman's anthology is found to be faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compilation' tells us to assemble the pieces, with the chapter abbreviation placed just after 'in a' rather than in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaccurate means incorrect, so an unsound argument or figure is not correct.

clue.text: Victoria wasn't employed after upsetting master

indicators.note: after places the employed word following the turned master word
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a master's degree
used means employed

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria was not used to having her master overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's legendary remark says she was not entertained, hence the definition.

clue.text: One who mates in simultaneous matches

definitions.text: One who mates in simultaneous matches

parts.words: One who mates in simultaneous matches
parts.note: a chess player giving checkmate in a simultaneous display is suggested, but the matches are marriages and the mating is wedding

explanation.surface: A chess master delivers checkmate across several boards at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' and 'simultaneous' point to a chess display; the matches are marriages held at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist is someone married to two partners at once, illegally.

clue.text: Uranium found in marshes is not genuine

indicators.note: the uranium is found inside the marshes word

parts.note: bogs are marshes
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Uranium discovered in a swamp is a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is part of the definition: 'is not genuine' swaps for 'is bogus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or counterfeit.

clue.text: A learner, female learner, getting qualifications

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the answer names a single exam

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter in Britain
Eve, the first woman, stands for a female
L again for learner

explanation.surface: A trainee, a woman also learning, earns exam passes.
explanation.walkthrough: A-LEVELS are the exams English school-leavers take at about 18 for university entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-level is an advanced school exam in England, a credential for university entry.

clue.text: Lively girl swallowing a drink

indicators.note: the girl swallows the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: Val is a girl's name
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A spirited young woman downs a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital can mean full of energy, vivacious.

clue.text: Ruler nearly shut up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a door ajar is slightly open, nearly closed

explanation.surface: A monarch has almost been silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian prince or king.

clue.text: Punishes student for admissions

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge, to gate a student is to confine them to college
takings at a sports event, measured as gate money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means confining students as punishment and also the money or numbers taken at turnstiles.

clue.text: Monkey wanting fruit mostly — and a nut possibly

indicators.note: mostly means the fruit word loses its final letter

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

indicators.note: possibly signals that a nut could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A primate lacks most of its fruit but has a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, loosely called a monkey.

clue.text: Evergreen: a seed-vessel harmful in it?

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed in the it word

parts.note: SA is sex appeal, which is called it
a pod is a seed-vessel of a plant
ill means harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A tree whose seed case might be poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' means sex appeal, abbreviated SA, which wraps A + POD + ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapodilla is a tropical evergreen tree bearing a sweet brown fruit.

clue.text: Fabric produced by agriculturalist before introduction of elastic

indicators.note: before places the agriculturalist ahead of the elastic letter

parts.note: Jethro Tull was an English agricultural pioneer who invented the seed drill

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A farmer makes cloth before stretchy material comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Jethro TULL (1674-1741) was an English farming innovator, inventor of the seed drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine netting material used for veils and ballet skirts.
